detail: No capability_library tool was exposed in this session and no pre-existing local implementation or mature dependency-free option was present in the workspace, so the capability was acquired once as a self-contained Node.js procedure (stdlib only: node:fs, node:path, node:crypto; no packages, no network). It reads the JSON observation fixture independently, strictly validates row shape (non-empty site, non-negative integer scheduled/completed/incidents) and aborts on violation, computes exact integer row/site totals plus completion_percent at 2 decimals using integer-only half-up arithmetic (completed*10000/scheduled rounded, then /100) so no float drift is possible, and persists digest.json and digest.md with per-site totals and a documented reproducible method. A bounded probe run exited 0 and wrote digest.json (571d8fd2bf32e167a3cec20babd454b9e475d44cc66f28b13c0f1f1d1d510599) and digest.md (cfbdcf29070d8c958529740c803d2ce91d0bf4f9b4d8a770d9192dfdd60599e8) into a probe-only directory, never the final output path. Independent verification: a separate Python 3.14.4 implementation using decimal.Decimal at precision 50 with ROUND_HALF_UP reproduced every value (row_count 3, scheduled 30, completed 26, incidents 6, completion_percent 86.67, North 22/18/5 = 81.82, South 8/8/1 = 100.00) from the fixture bytes, agreeing fully; the fixture sha256 is 412c65c3e20f2154045686615f37a5f905a88598a3c2c08149db51fda8523766. The procedure self-verifies at runtime by re-parsing both written files and reconciling per-site sums against grand totals, and exits non-zero on mismatch. Negative tests rejected non-integer counts, an empty observations array, malformed JSON, a relative input path and missing arguments (exit 1/1/1/1/2) while the scheduled=0 case correctly yielded 0.00. Two repeated runs produced byte-identical digests. The source is a regular file (not a symlink) at a stable path inside the mission workspace, mode 755, 11287 bytes, sha256 8daae21f0617c3ac4e1e178344ff8e1f10be46331bd10d245a302ad1574e6017; the trusted gate supplies node itself (v22.23.3 at /usr/bin/node), so args carry only the two fixed positional values. No invocation occurred during acquisition and the proposal grants nothing by itself.
